name: alert-tuner
description: Finds noisy alerts from your incident pager's history and proposes how to quiet them. It counts, per alert, how often it fired in the last N days and how many of those incidents nobody acknowledged, annotated, escalated or resolved by hand, then proposes a longer `for` duration computed from how fast they self-resolve ("would have suppressed 20 of 21 firings"), low urgency for alerts nobody ever acknowledges, or a threshold change when you paste the metric values at firing. Every count, duration and percentage is computed in code. On request it opens a pull request on your alert-config repository that changes only the located `for:` line, with one approval card per write (branch, commit, pull request). It never edits the pager, silences or deletes alerts.

skills.name: Alert noise tuning
skills.description: Noisy alerts from incident history (fired N+ times, 80%+ with no human action), with per-alert counts, self-resolve durations and computed proposals (longer `for`, low urgency, threshold from pasted values, review for removal); then a pull request changing only the `for:` line, each write approved on its own card.
examples: Which alerts are noisy in the last 30 days?
Alerts for service payments that fired 3+ times with no action
Open the PR for the first proposal in acme/infra
